advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a logger.warning/error inside _force_process_exit (or before os._exit) recording that the hard-shutdown deadline tripped, so a forced-down orphaned-thread event is observable and alarmable.
evidence: _force_process_exit body is only `os._exit(code)` with no `logger.warning/error` before it — the forced-down case leaves no trace in logs
Ticket AC4: 'A health/liveness signal distinguishes "listener closed, process alive" from healthy, so this state alarms instead of presenting as a silent 502.'
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:116: `timer = threading.Timer(grace, _force_process_exit)` — armed with no non-zero code
Ticket AC4 wants this abnormal state to alarm; a 0 exit code is indistinguishable from clean shutdown to the orchestrator
advisory.finding: The hard-exit path emits no log record: _force_process_exit calls os._exit(code) directly with no logger call, so when the daemon deadline actually trips (the zombie/orphaned-thread incident case) there is no operator-visible signal that the process was force-killed rather than exiting cleanly. This is precisely the state the ticket's AC4 asks to be made distinguishable/alarmable.
merged_from: The forced kill uses exit code 0 (_force_process_exit default code=0, and _arm_hard_shutdown passes no code), so a process force-terminated because an orphaned OS thread hung shutdown reports SUCCESS to the container/orchestrator — identical to a clean exit, erasing the distinguishing signal.
scenarios: A genuinely-hung orphaned asyncio.to_thread review keeps the process alive past the 5s grace; the timer fires os._exit and the container disappears with no log line explaining why.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _force_process_exit, log a warning (e.g. logger.warning('review-bot: hard-shutdown deadline elapsed; force-exiting orphaned to_thread review', ...)) before calling os._exit(code).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the 5s grace comfortably exceeds any legitimate post-lifespan teardown, or gate the hard-exit on an actual liveness signal (pending tasks / surviving non-daemon thread) rather than an unconditional wall-clock deadline.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:264: `_arm_hard_shutdown(_HARD_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS)` armed unconditionally, not conditioned on `tasks` still pending or a live to_thread thread
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:116: `threading.Timer(grace, _force_process_exit)` fires after `grace` seconds regardless of whether a thread is actually orphaned

comment claims it 'only ever fires when the process is still alive grace seconds after ... an orphaned OS thread is holding it up' but the timer cannot distinguish an orphan from a merely-slow legitimate teardown
advisory.finding: The 5s grace is a fixed wall-clock deadline armed unconditionally at the end of shutdown, not gated on an orphaned thread actually existing; any post-lifespan teardown that legitimately takes longer than the grace (e.g. a to_thread offload that would finish at 6s, or slow default-executor drain) is also hard-killed via os._exit, effectively SIGKILL-equivalent for that in-flight work.
scenarios: A review's blocking to_thread work is nearly done and would complete at ~6s of teardown; the 5s deadline force-exits it mid-write instead of letting it finish, discarding work the drain intended to preserve.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a clean lifespan shutdown (no orphaned to_thread thread; worker/reconciler honor cancellation promptly) leaves the `_force_process_exit` seam un-called (`exits == []`).
evidence: app.py:256-264 comment: 'a clean teardown exits before it fires (the timer evaporates with the process), and only a genuinely-orphaned thread trips it into a hard exit'
The only new positive test (`test_shutdown_forces_process_exit_when_an_orphaned_to_thread_review_outlives_cancel`) asserts `exits == [0]` for the HUNG case only: tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:2285

ABSENCE: search for `force_process_exit` in the test file returns only the autouse no-op neutralizer (line 67) and the hung-case recorder (line 2237); no test asserts `exits == []` after a clean shutdown

The autouse fixture patches the seam to a no-op for all other tests (tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:67), so no existing test can observe a spurious force-down on a clean shutdown either — leaving the must-NOT-fire half wholly uncovered
blocking.finding: No test covers the clean-teardown half of the self-distinguishing contract: that a normal lifespan shutdown with no orphaned to_thread thread does NOT call `_force_process_exit`. Only the hung-thread firing case is tested, so a regression that fires the hard exit unconditionally (e.g. grace set to 0, timer not daemonized/not evaporating, or firing on every clean shutdown) would go undetected — the design claim 'a clean teardown exits before it fires / the daemon timer evaporates with the process' is asserted only in prose.
scenarios: A future edit sets `_HARD_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 0.0` or arms the timer before the bounded gather, force-exiting on every clean deploy restart; the suite stays green.
The daemon flag is dropped or the fire condition is inverted so the process is killed even when drain+cancel completed cleanly.
blocking.suggested_fix: Mirror the hung-case test but with a `_worker` that honors cancellation immediately (no to_thread offload / short sleep), record the seam, run the lifespan to a clean shutdown, then poll past `_HARD_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` and assert the recorded exits list is empty — proving the daemon timer evaporated without firing.
